name: Information Systems Archive
description: Off-repository archive mirror (shipping order S-2) of Sea Dog Terminal's data archive, the lineage now served by Payload Terminal V0. What matters here is the UNRECONSTRUCTABLE class: UN Comtrade captures. Comtrade keeps one version per dataset and revises in place, so a lost capture is a knowledge state that cannot be recovered from anywhere, including UNSD. The mirror holds the 2026-08-27 Comtrade retrievals for copper ore (HS 2603) and refined copper (HS 7403) reporters Chile, Peru, China, DRC and Indonesia, the comtrade-* served snapshots and data-availability vintages, plus refetchable-at-risk Open Ownership captures and refetchable USGS MCS, CFTC, Yahoo, Westmetall and EDGAR snapshots, every file indexed in MANIFEST.json with a sha256 and durability class and checked by verify.mjs. It is a second GitHub repository guarding against repo-level accidents, not a provider-independent backup; it must never be treated as current data (byte identity is coverage for divergence, not currency) and never be edited by hand.

capabilities.label: Read the durability manifest
capabilities.description: sea-dog-terminal/data-archive/MANIFEST.json lists every mirrored file with path, sha256, bytes and durability class (counts: 14 unreconstructable, 8 refetchable_at_risk, 6 refetchable, 1 documentation). Generated upstream by scripts/archive-manifest.mjs; the label a pruner needs in a year.
capabilities.provenance: generated by Payload/Sea Dog Terminal scripts/archive-manifest.mjs

capabilities.label: Verify the mirror against its manifest
capabilities.description: `node sea-dog-terminal/verify.mjs` hashes every manifest entry under sea-dog-terminal/ and prints `OK: N files verified` (exit 0) or `MISMATCH <path>` lines and `FAILED: n mismatches` (exit 1). Detects corruption or divergence in the mirror; does not detect staleness.

capabilities.label: Read unreconstructable UN Comtrade raw captures
capabilities.description: sea-dog-terminal/data-archive/comtrade/<retrieval-date>/<reporter>-<hs>-<flow>-<year>.json holds the verbatim Comtrade API response ({elapsedTime, count, data[...]} rows with reporterCode, partnerCode, cmdCode, flowCode, qty, netWgt, primaryValue...) for each successful live retrieval, keyed by retrieval date and request key. Eleven files for 2026-08-27 (152/604/360 x 2603 exports 2017-2024; 156 x 2603/7403 imports 2023; 180 x 7403 exports 2023); five are the 11-byte empty-result body.

capabilities.label: Read the served Comtrade snapshots and flow vintages
capabilities.description: sea-dog-terminal/src/data/economy/snapshots/comtrade-copper.json, comtrade-flow-vintages.json and comtrade-da.json (unreconstructable class) are the vintages the terminal serves from; comtrade-da.json records per reporter/period firstReleased and lastReleased so `as_known_then` blindness before the held version's release date is labelled rather than silent.
capabilities.provenance: UN Comtrade getDA and getData captures retrievedAt 2026-08-27

capabilities.label: Read refetchable-at-risk Open Ownership captures
capabilities.description: sea-dog-terminal/data-archive/openownership/2026-08-27/: S3 export listings (s3-list.xml, s3-public-exports.xml), BODS statement samples (control-glencore-sample.jsonl, match-antamina.jsonl), register search pages (search-antamina.html, search-collahuasi.html) and scan-summary.txt (statements=32813462 antamina=1 collahuasi=0 glencore_control=53) from a frozen 2023 export of a retired product.
capabilities.provenance: Open Ownership BODS public S3 export, captured 2026-08-27

capabilities.label: Read refetchable economy snapshots
capabilities.description: sea-dog-terminal/src/data/economy/snapshots/: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024/2025 world copper and 2025 aluminium (.ts), cftc-copper-1yr.json, yahoo-hg-10y.json, sec-edgar-recon.json (refetchable) and westmetall-lme-stocks.json (refetchable_at_risk, single republisher). Loss costs a re-fetch, not a vintage.
capabilities.provenance: USGS MCS, CFTC, Yahoo Finance, Westmetall, SEC EDGAR captures

capabilities.label: Restore the archive into a terminal checkout
capabilities.description: Documented restore path: clone this repo, run verify.mjs, copy sea-dog-terminal/data-archive/ and sea-dog-terminal/src/data/economy/snapshots/ over the same paths in a checkout of the main repository, then run `npx vitest run src/lib/economy/archiveManifest.test.ts` there (green = byte-identical). Executed once at mirror creation (ledger phase 36). Overwrites files in another repository.
capabilities.side_effects: overwrites data-archive/ and snapshots/ in the target checkout

capabilities.label: Refresh the mirror after an archival
capabilities.description: Update cadence: mirror after every archival (any new day-directory under data-archive/comtrade/). The main repository's CI verifies its own manifest; this mirror is refreshed manually or by operator automation. No script exists here; the refresh is a copy plus commit.
capabilities.side_effects: commits new capture files and MANIFEST.json to this repository

relations.description: Confirmed by docs: the restore path copies sea-dog-terminal/data-archive/ and src/data/economy/snapshots/ over the same paths in a checkout of the main repository (Sea-Dog-OSIRIS-Terminal-V0, the terminal lineage now catalogued as payload-terminal) and validates with its archiveManifest.test.ts; the archive supplies the unreconstructable Comtrade vintages back to the terminal when they are lost. Executed once at mirror creation (ledger phase 36).

Inferred from docs: every file here originates in the terminal's data-archive/ and snapshots/ (the Comtrade adapter writes captures there before parsing) and MANIFEST.json is generated by the terminal's scripts/archive-manifest.mjs; the mirror has no capture or manifest tooling of its own and cannot refresh without the terminal.

reference.spatial: Carries trade geography as Comtrade reporter and partner country codes (Chile, Peru, China, DRC, Indonesia and their partners) for copper ore and refined copper flows; no coordinates.
reference.temporal: Vintage archive: captures keyed by retrieval date (2026-08-27) over reporting years 2017-2024, with firstReleased/lastReleased per dataset so as_known_then can be labelled; the mirror is only as current as its last manual refresh.
open_questions: The README names the source as Sea-Dog-OSIRIS-Terminal-V0 (formerly Notations-OSIRIS-Overwatch-Engine); the catalog treats that lineage as payload-terminal (image sea-dog-payload-terminal-v0). Confirm they are the same repository.
Only one capture day (2026-08-27) is mirrored; has any archival since then been mirrored, and who owns the refresh cadence?
Five Comtrade captures are 11-byte empty-result bodies; are these genuine empty datasets or failed retrievals archived as vintages?
No provider-independent copy exists; the mirror protects only against repo-level accidents on the same GitHub account.

corpus.holding: The 2026-08-27 UN Comtrade retrievals for copper ore (HS 2603) and refined copper (HS 7403) from reporters Chile, Peru, China, DRC and Indonesia, plus served snapshots, data-availability vintages and refetchable-at-risk captures, every file indexed in MANIFEST.json with a sha256 and a durability class.

COR-001.note: The holding is enumerated file by file with a durability class per entry.

COR-002.note: A mirror of another system's captures. It holds a corpus but owns no domain's canonical state, and says so: byte identity is coverage for divergence, not currency.

COR-003.note: Every file carries its sha256 and the capture it came from.

COR-004.note: Captures are keyed by retrieval date over reporting years 2017-2024, with firstReleased/lastReleased per dataset so as_known_then can be labelled.

COR-005.note: The mirror answers from files; there is no query surface to refuse from, and staleness is signalled only in prose.

COR-006.note: An archive admits nothing: it receives captures produced by the terminal's tooling and must never be edited by hand.

COR-007.note: The whole point of the node: Comtrade revises in place, so captures are archived and sha256-verified before anything parses them.

COR-008.note: Files are sha256-indexed in a manifest, but the manifest itself is not hash-linked or signed, so a consistent rewrite of both would not be detectable.

COR-009.note: The archive renders nothing and has no downstream state to write to.

COR-010.note: Must never be treated as current data, and never edited by hand.
